title: Amendment No. 2, Services Agreement 2023-2024 - My School RD, Inc. - Nutrition Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 2, Services Agreement 2023-2024 by and between the District and My School RD, Inc., Wrightwood, CA, for the latter to participate in a monthly virtual meeting to provide guidance to OUSD staff and answer questions related to special diets, how to accommodate new students and menu changes, including updates on carb counts and allergens; provide advice on new students with complex conditions via email as needed, for the unchanged term of July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, in the additional amount of $2,400.00, increasing the Agreement not to exceed amount from $87,500.00 to $89,900.00. title: Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement - Touro University - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement (MOU or Agreement) for an Intern Partnership Program and Practica Program - applying to credentials in K-12 Teaching, including Multiple Subjects, Single Subjects, Designated Subjects, and Special Education Categories, including Added or Supplementary Authorizations; including Pupil Personnel Services in Communicative Sciences & Disorders, Mental Health & Wellness, Counseling & Guidance, Educational Therapy, Administration, and other Pupil Personnel Services credentials and certifications, as may be specified; including Fieldwork Experience for Master of Arts or Science and other Graduate-Level Degrees or Certifications with Emphasis in Pupil Personnel Services; including Fieldwork Experience for Pre-Credential Candidate Undergraduate Students - is entered into by and between Oakland University School District (District or OUSD), a public school district in the State of California, County of Alameda, and Touro University (University or TU) [Vallejo, CA], a California nonprofit, private university - for the term July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2029, at no cost to the District other than for Teacher Interns who are deemed District employees and are paid from District funds associated with said employment.
headline: Renews Touro University's teacher and counselor intern partnership at no cost through 2029
summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Touro University sets up an intern and practica (supervised fieldwork) program for teaching credentials, special education, and pupil personnel services such as counseling, mental health and educational therapy. It also covers fieldwork for graduate and undergraduate students. It runs July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2029 at no cost to the district, except pay for Teacher Interns who are district employees.

Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 3, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and Mar Con Builders, Inc., Oakland, CA, which includes PCO's 29 through 34, for additional changes that require:1·
See PCO #29 for the planting of 4 new trees and installing irrigation due to CALGreen code & DSA requirements.
See PCO #30 for furnishing and installing fence and gates at four locations due to safety concerns.
See PCO #31 for replacing the existing sink @ unisex restroom with an ADA wall mounted lavatory sink.
See PCO #32 for location description changes of the fire alarm devices due to missing signage. See PCO #33 for added fire alarm devices due to restrooms missing detection.
See PCO #34 for added fire alarm devices at closets and portables B & D;
for the Kaiser Child Development Center Site Improvements Project, in the additional amount of $166,038.00, increasing the not to exceed amount of the Agreement from $6,781,918.00 to $6,947,95600. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $166,038 for site fixes at Mar Con Builders' Kaiser Child Development Center project
summary: Change Order No. 3 covers six preliminary change orders (PCOs 29 through 34): planting four trees and irrigation to meet code, new fence and gates for safety, an accessible restroom sink, and added or relocated fire alarm devices. It adds $166,038 to the contract, which was $6,781,918. The printed new total, "$6,947,95600", looks misprinted.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, Agreement for Architectural Services – HKIT Architects – Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park & Sherman Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, Agreement for Architectural Services by and between the District and HKIT Architects, Oakland CA, for the latter to provide additional architectural and engineering services which include portable relocation, main building modernization, and new classroom building, as described in the proposal dated May17, 2024, attached to this Amendment in Exhibit A, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park & Sherman Project, in an additional not-to-exceed amount of $3,275,806.00, which includes a $294,164.00 not-to-exceed contingency and a $40,000 not-to-exceed amount for reimbursable expenses, increasing the Agreement’s not to exceed amount from $1,104,910.00 to $4,380,716.00, and extending the term of the Agreement from September 15, 2022 through May 31, 2024 to September 30, 2028, (an additional 1,583 calendar days).  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $3.28M and four more years to HKIT Architects' Melrose Leadership Academy and Sherman design deal
summary: This amendment adds architectural and engineering services for portable relocation, main building modernization and a new classroom building. It adds up to $3,275,806 (including a $294,164 contingency and $40,000 for reimbursable expenses), raising the contract limit from $1,104,910 to $4,380,716. It also extends the end date from May 31, 2024 to September 30, 2028.
schools: Melrose Leadership Academy at Maxwell Park; Sherman
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Mar Con Builders, Inc. – Bella Vista Child Development Center Fire & Intrusion Alarm Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Bid Award, rejecting all others, if any, and an Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and Mar Con Builders, Inc., Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide construction services which include furnishing and installing new fire and intrusion alarm systems, test and removal of the existing system for the Bella Vista Child Development Center Fire & Intrusion Alarm Project, in the total amount of $811,391.00, which includes a general contingency allowance of $30,000.00, as the lowest responsive, responsible bidder, with the work anticipated to commence on June 27, 2024, and scheduled to last for seventy-four days (74), with an anticipated ending of September 9, 2024.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
funding_source: Fund 21 Building Fund Measure Y Fund 25 Capital Facilities Fund
headline: Awards Mar Con Builders $811,391 for new fire and intrusion alarms at Bella Vista Child Development Center
summary: Mar Con Builders was the lowest responsive, responsible bidder to install new fire and intrusion alarm systems at Bella Vista Child Development Center and test and remove the existing system. The total of $811,391 includes a $30,000 general contingency allowance. Work is expected to start June 27, 2024 and last 74 days, ending about September 9, 2024.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Agreement for Maintenance – Johnson Controls Fire Protection, LP – Coliseum College Preparatory Academy Interim Housing - Division of Facilities Planning and Management

title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – DecoTech Systems – 955 High Street VOIP Cabling Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of the Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and DecoTech Systems, Walnut Creek, CA., for the latter to provide construction services, which consists of the installation of new data cables to various locations within the 955 High Street Facilities and Buildings & Grounds offices; replacing existing network cabinets and re-routing existing data cables through new cabbing pathways, for the 955 High Street VOIP Cabling Project, in an amount not to exceed $33,660.00, with the work scheduled to commence on June 27, 2024, and scheduled to last until October 31, 2024.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Pays DecoTech Systems up to $33,660 for new network cabling at the 955 High Street offices
summary: DecoTech Systems will install new data cables to various locations in the 955 High Street Facilities and Buildings & Grounds offices, replace network cabinets and re-route existing data cables through new pathways. This is the 955 High Street internet-based phone (VoIP) cabling project. The limit is $33,660, with work from June 27, 2024 to October 31, 2024.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: General Services Agreement – Lowe Consulting Group, Inc. – Facilities Planning & Management Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a General Services Agreement by and between the District and Lowe Consulting Group, Inc., Oakland CA, for the latter to provide Project Labor Agreement (PLA) services, assisting the District with managing labor relations, coordinating the PLA’s innovative workforce development and employment programs, and monitoring and reporting on the efficacy of the PLA, more specifically described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the Facilities Planning and Management, total not-to-exceed in the amount of $183,810.00, which includes a not-to-exceed amount of $167,000.00, for Basic Services, and a not-to-exceed amount of $16,710.00 for Additional Services, as the selected consultant, with work scheduled to commence on June 27, 2024, and scheduled to last until June 30, 2025.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Pays Lowe Consulting Group up to $183,810 for Project Labor Agreement services on district construction
summary: Lowe Consulting Group will help the district manage labor relations under its Project Labor Agreement (PLA), coordinate the PLA's workforce development and employment programs, and monitor and report on how well it works. The stated limit is $183,810, described as $167,000 for basic services and $16,710 for additional services. The work runs from June 27, 2024 to June 30, 2025.
source_issue: The stated total not-to-exceed of $183,810.00 is $100 more than its two parts, $167,000.00 for Basic Services and $16,710.00 for Additional Services, which add to $183,710.00.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
